answer: Locking a refundable stake per identity makes fake accounts expensive: each agent must escrow value that is slashed if it misbehaves, so a Sybil attacker pays linearly per fake. A public beacon ledger records every agent's verified work history, and like a reef that only grows where real coral settles, reputation accrues slowly from attested tasks. A marble identity token, earned only after repeated verified contributions, cannot be copied cheaply — forging a hundred marbles costs a hundred stakes, so mass fakery stops paying.
